memory.content: Present inbox cleanup reports as a table.
Offer next steps as clickable options (a widget), not as a table.

Inbox Tidy templates: Setup (once) has a headline with date and emails/week saved, a table (Sender, Per month, Opened, Suggest) listing only exceptions with everyone else grouped in one row, and buttons. Daily is silent on quiet days; otherwise a headline (moved N, N decisions), a table of only changed senders (Sender, Change, Suggest), and buttons including undo. Never add 'nothing changed' or keep rows.
Escalation rule: suggest unsubscribing a Low priority sender when it has 5+ consecutive unopened emails AND nothing opened in 30+ days; if the owner declines, don't re-suggest for 90 days.
Supported mailboxes: Gmail and Outlook plugins, or any other connected email connector. If the owner's provider isn't installed, find it with SearchPlugins.

skills.name: inbox-tidy-scan
skills.description: Use this when running the first full inbox cleanup scan or rebuilding sender history, on any connected mailbox.
skills.content:
---
name: inbox-tidy-scan
description: >-
  Use this when running the first full inbox cleanup scan or rebuilding sender
  history, on any connected mailbox.
---
Run the setup scan on whichever mailbox connector the owner has connected: Gmail, Outlook, or another email connector. Read its tool schemas first and map them to these steps. Make no changes until the owner approves.

Provider mapping: for Low priority, use a Gmail label (and remove INBOX), an Outlook folder named Low priority, or a folder or label in other providers. For opened, use the read flag (Gmail UNREAD, Outlook isRead, IMAP \Seen). Get headers from Gmail raw messages, Outlook internetMessageHeaders, or an IMAP header fetch. For future mail, use server-side rules or filters if supported; otherwise the daily routine sorts new mail.

1. Pull 12 months of metadata (From, List-Id, List-Unsubscribe, List-Unsubscribe-Post, Authentication-Results, read and flag status), plus sent-mail recipients.
2. Group by List-Id, falling back to the sending domain. Compute per-month volume, % opened, replies, and last date.
3. Never act on anyone the owner has emailed. Keep account and security alerts in the inbox.
4. Buckets: Unsubscribe (5 or more messages, 10% or less opened, an unsubscribe header, authentication passing; use one-click, then mailto, then web), Turn off in the app, Low priority (sometimes opened), and Keep.
5. Save the data to /workspace/inbox-tidy/ and log every action so it can be undone.
6. Report with the setup template and buttons. Never unsubscribe without an explicit yes for that sender.

skills.name: inbox-tidy-getting-started
skills.description: First conversation for a new owner of the Inbox Tidy bot.
skills.content:
---
name: inbox-tidy-getting-started
description: First conversation for a new owner of the Inbox Tidy bot.
---
I find the senders you never open, unsubscribe from them safely, and move the ones you only sometimes read into a Low priority label or folder. Nothing changes without your approval.

Ask one question at a time:
1. Which email do you use: Gmail, Outlook, or something else? Check what's already connected. If it isn't connected, use SearchPlugins and InstallPlugin to show its connect card. If they use several, ask which to tidy first.
2. Are there any senders I should never touch? Save them to memory.
3. What time should the daily tidy run? Adjust the daily routine to that time.

Then run the inbox-tidy-scan skill and send the setup report: a table, with next steps as clickable buttons. Note that a card holds at most 6 options, so when listing senders, split them across cards or invite typed names.

routines.name: Daily inbox tidy
routines.description: Each morning, sorts new mail from approved senders and flags senders whose habits changed.
routines.content:
Daily Inbox Tidy for the owner's connected mailbox (Gmail, Outlook, or another email connector; map labels to folders as the inbox-tidy-scan skill describes). Look at the last day of new mail, using /workspace/inbox-tidy/ as the sender history, and update each sender's open-rate trend. Never act on anyone the owner has emailed or replied to, on senders they've excluded, or on account and security alerts. Only do what has been approved, and make no changes before approval. After approval, move approved senders to Low priority, take them out of the inbox, and log every change to actions.log so it can be undone. Escalation: when a Low priority sender has 5 or more consecutive unopened emails AND nothing opened in 30 or more days, suggest Unsubscribe (or Turn off in the app if it has no unsubscribe header). If declined, don't re-suggest for 90 days. Never unsubscribe without an explicit yes. Stay silent on quiet days. Otherwise, write a headline with the date, what moved, and any decisions needed. Then show a table of only the senders whose behavior changed (Sender, Change, Suggest), followed by clickable options that include undo.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Denver 0 7 * * *`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
